Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — following up with a concise commissioning plan so we can align on verification gates and a rehearsal window before the formal swap. Attached is a first-pass capacity matrix I filled from the numbers you gave (orbitbio_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx). Key asks:

- Are you comfortable with a 4-hour blackout window for the final routing cutover (we recommend a short, scheduled window to flush caches and swap DNS)?

Proposed near-term schedule (tentative):
- Wed 11/29: staging stress run (clients simulate 50–75% traffic)
- Thu 11/30: canary swap (5% production -> dedicated for 2h)
- Mon 12/4: final cutover rehearsal (full smoke + fallback test)

Aditya & Karthik — can you review the attached matrix and flag any GPU SKU/packing issues? Monica, can you advise on acceptance criteria we should require from OrbitBio SRE before we greenlight the canary?

Claire — if these dates look plausible on your side I’ll push a formal calendar invite and a short runbook for the rehearsal.

Thanks, Camila — the matrix looks like a good starting point. Quick clarifications: 

- Peak concurrent: our telemetry shows sustained peaks at ~130–150 qps during our morning batch window (08:00–10:30 PT). Bursts up to 220 qps for short periods.
- Latency SLO: p99 target is 150 ms for the scoring endpoint. We can accept a short p99 bump during the rehearsal if it's clearly documented.
- Models: we plan to start on quantized-medium for cheaper tails, but we will need the large float variant available as a fallback for high-quality scoring runs.

The team prefers to avoid a long blackout window: can we do a 60–90 minute window instead? If the swap requires more time, we’d prefer staged traffic drainage.

We can make 11/29–12/4 work, but is it possible to shift the staging stress run to 11/30 and do the canary on 12/1? Our infra leads have a planned maintenance on 11/28.

Claire Hsu

Claire — thanks for the numbers, that helps. Technical notes from infra side: 

- GPU SKUs: for the requested p99 and burst profile I recommend a mixed pool: 4x A100L40 (for the large float fallback) + 12x A100Q20 (quantized path). That gives us headroom for concurrent KV cache and batch spikes.
- Packing: we should reserve 20% of GPU memory for KV cache/latency headroom — the matrix should reflect that (I’ll update).
- Warm swap approach: prefer staged drain + connection TTL reduce rather than DNS-only blackout; kube-proxy + edge routing can shift without full DNS TTL propagation. This allows a 60–90 minute procedural window rather than a hard 4-hour blackout.
- Stress tests: we’ll need a replay dataset and a synthetic burst harness. Suggest we run two 60-min stress runs: one at 75% expected peak, one at 120% burst.

I’ve created a short runbook draft and added a checklist to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1OrbitBioCutoverPlan (permissions set to OrbitBio + Redwood infra).

Thanks all — based on inbound numbers and Aditya’s SKU recommendation I sketched a concrete timeline and gating matrix below. I’m proposing slightly different sequencing to reduce risk:

- Tue 11/28: final infra freeze (we’ll avoid this date per Claire’s note) -> MOVED
- Thu 11/30, 09:00–12:00 PT: Staging stress runs (two sessions: 09:00–10:15 at 75% and 10:45–12:00 at 120% burst). Owners: Redwood infra + OrbitBio SRE.
- Fri 12/1, 10:00–12:00 PT: Canary (5% prod -> dedicated) + smoke checks. If green, rollback window closes at 12:30.
- Mon 12/4, 02:00–03:30 PT: Full rehearsal (routing swap + fallback exercise). We picked a small overnight window to reduce impact.
- Tue 12/5, 06:00–07:30 PT: Final cutover slot (60–90 minutes). This is the planned production swap.

Gates to proceed to Canary:
1) Staging stress run: no p99 > 250 ms sustained for >5 min.
2) Error budget consumption during stress run < 1.5x normal.
3) Runbook walkthrough completed and owners assigned.

Fallbacks and automatic rollbacks:
- If p99 crosses 400 ms for >3 minutes we initiate automatic 100% traffic fallback to Hosted via policy.

Monica — can you confirm acceptance criteria doc and on-call escalation matrix? I’ll add the finalized timeline to the cutover_playbook_draft.docx attachment.

Karthik Iyer
Senior PM, Customer Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
